It sets a tariff-rate quota for 100,000 United Kingdom automobiles each year at a 10 percent tariff, and it lowers the tariff on certain United Kingdom automotive parts used in United Kingdom automobiles to 10 percent. It also removes certain tariffs on some United Kingdom aerospace products and tells the Secretary of Commerce to later set tariff-rate quotas for United Kingdom aluminum and steel articles and their derivative articles.

14310.s: This order extends the delay on enforcing the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act for TikTok until September 17, 2025. During that time, the Department of Justice may not enforce the law or impose penalties for noncompliance, including distributing, maintaining, or updating covered applications. It also directs the Attorney General to issue guidance and letters saying there was no violation and no liability for covered conduct during the stated periods.

14311.s: This order creates a White House Office for Special Peace Missions. The office is meant to help bring about the end of conflict and strife around the world and to advance efforts aimed at ending ongoing conflicts abroad. It will be led by a Special Envoy for Peace Missions appointed by the President and will work with the Department of State, the Department of Defense, and other executive departments and agencies.

14312.s: This order revokes Syria sanctions by ending the national emergency and revoking several earlier executive orders related to Syria. It directs the Secretary of State, the Treasury, and Commerce to take additional steps, including removing sanctions on Syria, issuing waivers that allow some export controls and other restrictions to be relaxed, and implementing the order. It also waives or reviews some sanctions and designations under the Syria Accountability Act, the Chemical and Biological Weapons Control and Warfare Elimination Act, and counterterrorism authorities, and it directs steps at the United Nations on Syria-related sanctions relief.

14313.s:
This executive order creates the President's Make America Beautiful Again Commission. The commission will advise the President on conserving natural resources, improving conservation efforts, and expanding access to public lands, national parks, national forests, wildlife refuges, and outdoor recreation.

It also directs federal land management agencies to expand access for recreation, hunting, and fishing, cut bureaucratic delays, and encourage voluntary conservation. The order applies to federal land management agencies and to the officials named on the commission.

14314.s: This order tells the Secretary of the Interior to develop a plan to raise entrance fees and recreation pass fees for nonresidents at national parks. It also says increased fee revenue should be used to improve park infrastructure and enjoyment or access, and that services and affordability for United States residents should be improved. The order directs reviews of park maintenance, public use rules, and recreational access rules, and it says American residents should get preferential treatment under any remaining access rules. It also revokes a 2017 presidential memorandum about diversity and inclusion in public lands.

14315.s: This order directs the Treasury Department to enforce the end of clean electricity production and investment tax credits for wind and solar facilities. It also directs Treasury to carry out new foreign entity restrictions in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The Interior Department must review its rules and practices for any preference for wind and solar facilities and revise them if needed.

14316.s: This order extends a temporary suspension of certain reciprocal tariff rates until August 1, 2025. It affects goods from foreign trading partners covered by the suspended tariff headings. The separate tariff suspension for the People's Republic of China stays in effect and is not changed by this order.

14317.s: This order creates Schedule G in the excepted service for noncareer positions that are policy-making or policy-advocating and are normally subject to change during a Presidential transition. It says these appointments will be made under Schedule G, and it directs the Office of Personnel Management to adopt any needed rules to carry it out. It also says the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, when making Schedule G appointments, must consider whether people would be suitable exponents of the President's policies and must not consider their political affiliation or political activity.

14318.s: This order directs federal agencies to speed up permitting for certain data center projects and the infrastructure that supports them. It also tells agencies to look for ways to provide financial support, use federal land and resources, and identify Brownfield Sites, Superfund Sites, and military sites for these projects. The order applies to qualifying data center projects, related manufacturing projects, and project sponsors.

14319.s: This order directs federal agencies to buy only large language models that are truthful and politically neutral. It says these models should not manipulate responses to favor ideological dogmas such as DEI, and should be accurate about factual, historical, and scientific information. The order also directs OMB to issue guidance and tells agencies to add these requirements to federal contracts for large language models, with some exceptions for national security systems.

14320.s: This order directs the Department of Commerce to create an American AI Exports Program to support the development and deployment of United States full-stack AI export packages. Those packages can include hardware, data pipelines, AI models, security measures, and AI applications, and they must name target countries or regional blocs and follow U.S. export and investment rules. The order also directs federal agencies to coordinate financing tools, diplomacy, and technical help for selected priority AI export packages.

14321.s: This order directs federal agencies to take steps on homelessness, civil commitment, drug use, camping, loitering, and related public safety issues. It tells officials to seek changes to legal precedents and consent decrees, and to help state and local governments use civil commitment and treatment for some people with mental illness or substance use disorder. It also tells agencies to review grant programs, housing assistance, and health funding, including possible limits on support for certain programs and more data sharing with law enforcement.

14322.s: This order says college sports should be preserved and, where possible, expanded. It directs federal officials to support more scholarship and roster spots in women’s and other non-revenue sports, and to work on policies about athlete pay and legal protections for college athletics. It also directs agencies to look at the status of college athletes and to consult about the role college sports play in developing athletes for international competition.

14323.s: This order declares a national emergency over actions of the Government of Brazil that it says threaten the national security, foreign policy, and economy of the United States. It imposes an additional 40 percent duty on certain products from Brazil imported into the United States, with some exceptions. The Secretary of State must monitor the situation and report to Congress, and the order allows changes if Brazil retaliates or takes steps to address the emergency.

14324.s: This order ends duty-free de minimis treatment for shipments of articles not covered by 50 U.S.C. 1702(b), no matter their value, country of origin, or how they are sent. Most such shipments will now be subject to duties, taxes, fees, exactions, and charges, while international postal shipments will follow special duty rules until CBP sets a new entry process. It also sets duty methods for postal shipments and says the changes take effect for goods entered for consumption on or after August 29, 2025.

14325.s: This order raises the extra duty on certain products of Canada from 25 percent to 35 percent. It also says goods from Canada that are found to have been transshipped to evade duties will face a 40 percent duty, plus other fines or penalties. The Secretary of Homeland Security must keep monitoring the situation at the northern border and recommend more action if needed.

14326.s: This order changes the tariff rates on goods from certain foreign trading partners and updates the U.S. tariff schedule. Goods from trading partners not listed in Annex I will generally face an additional 10 percent duty, while goods from some listed partners will stay under the rates in Annex I until new agreements are reached. It also says goods found to have been transshipped to evade duties will face a 40 percent additional duty and other penalties.

14327.s: This order revokes a 2018 order and establishes the President's Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition. It also reestablishes the Presidential Fitness Test, which is to be administered by the Secretary of Health and Human Services with support from the Secretary of Education. The council will advise the President and recommend ways to expand youth sports, physical fitness, and good nutrition.

14328.s: This order creates a White House task force for the 2028 Summer Olympics. The task force will coordinate federal planning and response for security, transportation, and entry and exit processes, and it will help with visa processing and credentialing for foreign athletes, coaches, officials, and media personnel. It will also work with state and local partners and look for legal, logistical, or regulatory barriers that could affect federal support for the Games.

14329.s: This order says India is directly or indirectly importing Russian Federation oil and places an extra 25 percent duty on articles of India imported into the United States. The new duty applies to covered goods entered for consumption after the effective date, with some exceptions listed in the order. It also directs the Secretary of Commerce and other officials to monitor whether other countries are importing Russian Federation oil and to recommend further action if needed.

14330.s: This order directs the Secretary of Labor to review Department of Labor guidance on offering retirement funds that include alternative assets in 401(k) and other defined-contribution plans. It also directs the Secretary to consider rescinding a 2021 statement and to propose rules, regulations, or guidance on fiduciary duties, including possible safe harbors. The SEC is told to consider ways to help participants in these retirement plans access investments in alternative assets.

14331.s: This order says no American should be denied financial services because of protected beliefs, affiliations, or political views. It tells federal banking regulators to remove guidance that could lead to politicized or unlawful debanking and to review their rules and actions. It also tells some financial institutions to try to reinstate or notify customers who were denied services or payment processing because of such debanking. The Treasury Secretary and banking regulators must also review past practices and may take remedial action when allowed by law.

14332.s: This order directs federal agencies to strengthen review and oversight of federal grants. It requires agency leaders to review funding announcements and discretionary grants to make sure they fit agency priorities, the national interest, and the law. It also directs changes to grant rules so agencies can end discretionary grants for convenience in some cases, limit some administrative costs, and add new terms for future grants.

14333.s: This order says there is a crime emergency in the District of Columbia. It requires the Mayor to provide the Metropolitan Police Department for federal purposes to maintain law and order, protect federal buildings and property, and help the federal government function. It gives the Attorney General control over that authority and directs regular monitoring and updates.

14334.s: This order continues a suspension of a country-specific extra tariff rate on imports from the People's Republic of China until November 10, 2025. It affects articles from the PRC covered by the suspended tariff heading in the Harmonized Tariff Schedule. The Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the United States Trade Representative are directed to take the steps needed to carry it out.

14335.s: This order directs federal agencies to speed up reviews and approvals for commercial space launches, reentries, and spaceport development. It also tells the Secretary of Transportation to review and change launch and reentry rules, and tells the Secretary of Commerce to propose a faster process for some new space activities. It creates new leadership roles to support commercial space transportation and space commerce.

14336.s: This order directs Health and Human Services to fill the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve with active ingredients for certain critical drugs. It requires a list of about 26 critical drugs, a plan to ready the reserve repository, and a 6-month supply of the needed ingredients if funds are available. It also calls for an updated plan to obtain, store, and maintain a 6-month supply of ingredients for other essential medicines and for a proposal to open a second reserve repository in the United States.

14337.s: This order revokes Executive Order 14036, which had promoted competition in the American economy. It applies to executive departments, agencies, and the Office of Management and Budget only as described in the order’s general provisions.

14338.s: This order creates the "America by Design" initiative to improve the visual presentation and usability of federal services in digital and physical spaces. It also creates a National Design Studio and a Chief Design Officer to help with that work. Federal agencies must consult with the Chief Design Officer and work on initial results by July 4, 2026, including improving major websites and physical sites and updating the United States Web Design System.

14339.s: This order directs new steps to address the crime emergency in the District of Columbia. It tells federal officials to hire more Park Police and prosecutors, set up an online portal for people with law enforcement or other relevant backgrounds to apply to federal law enforcement jobs, and create specialized units for public safety and order. It also directs HUD to investigate possible non-compliance with crime-prevention and safety requirements in housing agreements, and directs Transportation to inspect federally funded transit services in the District of Columbia for conditions that endanger transit workers.

14340.s: This order directs federal officials in the District of Columbia to work to keep arrestees in federal custody as far as the law allows and to seek federal charges and pretrial detention when possible. It also tells the Attorney General to review Metropolitan Police Department policies and ask the Mayor to make changes if needed. The order has the Attorney General check whether the District still prohibits cash bail for certain serious crimes, and if so, agencies may take actions to press for policy changes.

14341.s: This order directs the Attorney General to prioritize enforcing federal criminal and civil laws against American flag desecration when it violates content-neutral laws and causes harm unrelated to expression. It also says agencies should refer possible state or local law violations to the proper authorities. The order directs immigration officials to deny, revoke, or seek removal of foreign nationals who have engaged in American flag-desecration activity when federal law allows it.

14342.s: This order says federal policies and resources should not be used to support state or local jurisdictions with cashless bail policies, to the extent allowed by law. It directs the Attorney General to list jurisdictions that have substantially eliminated cash bail for certain crimes that pose a clear threat to public safety and order. It also directs federal agencies to identify federal funds, including grants and contracts, that may be suspended or terminated for those jurisdictions, as allowed by law.

14343.s: This order excludes certain agencies and parts of agencies from the federal labor-management relations program because they are determined to do intelligence, counterintelligence, investigative, or national security work. It adds units in the Bureau of Reclamation that operate, manage, or maintain hydropower facilities, parts of the Department of Commerce, NASA, and the U.S. Agency for Global Media to those exclusions. It also extends the deadline for certain orders by the Secretaries of Defense and Veterans Affairs under a prior executive order.

14344.s: This order directs federal agencies to prefer classical and traditional architecture for certain federal public buildings, especially in the District of Columbia. It applies to federal courthouses, agency headquarters, certain other federal buildings, and some projects that cost or are expected to cost more than $50 million. It also tells the General Services Administration to update its policies, train staff with classical or traditional architecture experience, and give notice before approving certain nonpreferred designs.

14345.s: This order puts into effect parts of the United States-Japan agreement by changing tariffs on products from Japan. It sets a 15 percent tariff on nearly all Japanese imports unless a product already has a tariff of at least 15 percent, and it gives separate treatment for some aerospace, automobile, and automobile parts goods. It also allows some Japanese products, including certain natural resources and generic pharmaceuticals, to have a zero percent reciprocal tariff, while directing agencies to monitor Japan's commitments under the agreement.

14346.s: This order changes the scope of reciprocal tariffs and updates the list of goods that are excluded from them. It also sets procedures for the Secretary of Commerce and the United States Trade Representative to carry out framework agreements and final agreements with foreign trading partners, including making tariff changes when needed. The order affects goods imported into the United States and the agencies that implement trade and tariff rules.

14347.s: This order says the Department of Defense may be called the Department of War, and the Secretary of Defense may be called the Secretary of War in certain official settings. It also says subordinate officials may use similar secondary titles, and other executive departments and agencies must recognize those titles when used. Within 60 days, the Secretary of War must recommend actions needed to permanently rename the Department of Defense to the Department of War.

14349.s: This order creates an emergency board to investigate and report on disputes between the Long Island Rail Road Company and certain employees represented by labor organizations. The board must report to the President within 30 days of being created. For 120 days after the board is created, the parties may not change the conditions tied to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

14350.s: This order extends the delay on enforcement of the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act until December 16, 2025. During that time, the Department of Justice must not enforce the law or impose penalties for noncompliance, including for distributing, maintaining, or updating a foreign adversary controlled application. It also says the Justice Department will not take action over conduct that happened during the delay period or before this order.

14351.s: This order directs the creation of a "Gold Card" visa program for aliens who make an unrestricted gift to the Department of Commerce. The program would give an expedited process for an immigrant visa, and the gift would be treated as evidence of eligibility for certain visa and waiver categories. It also sets gift amounts, lets corporations or similar entities sponsor an individual, and requires agencies to set up the program and related fees.

14354.s: This order continues a list of federal advisory committees until September 30, 2027. The list includes committees on the White House, national security telecommunications, veterans small business development, HIV/AIDS, sports and nutrition, and several national monument advisory committees. It also says the heads of the named departments and agencies will carry out the President’s functions for these committees under the Federal Advisory Committee Act.

14355.s: This order directs the administration to use artificial intelligence to improve the diagnosis, treatment, cures, and prevention of pediatric cancer. It focuses on the Childhood Cancer Data Initiative, data platforms and tools, and research projects at National Cancer Institute-Designated Cancer Centers. It also calls for more investment in pediatric cancer research and care, better data sharing, and keeping patients and parents in control of their health information.

14356.s: This order limits federal civilian hiring by barring vacant positions from being filled or new positions from being created unless allowed by the order or by law. It requires agencies to use a Merit Hiring Plan, set up Strategic Hiring Committees, and prepare Annual Staffing Plans with quarterly updates. The order does not apply to several types of positions, including immigration enforcement, national security, public safety, and certain non-career jobs.

14357.s: This order lowers the extra ad valorem duty on covered goods from the People's Republic of China from 20 percent to 10 percent. It applies to goods entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption on or after November 10, 2025. The Secretary of Homeland Security must monitor the situation and may make needed tariff schedule changes to carry out the order.

14358.s: This order continues the suspension of the heightened reciprocal tariffs on imports from the People’s Republic of China until 12:01 a.m. eastern standard time on November 10, 2026. It carries out the economic and trade arrangement between the United States and the PRC by keeping those tariff changes in place. The Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Commerce, and the United States Trade Representative must keep monitoring the emergency conditions and the PRC’s commitments under the arrangement.

14359.s: This order directs the Health and Human Services Secretary to take steps to modernize state child welfare data and information systems. It also calls for a new "Fostering the Future" initiative and online platform to help people in foster care or leaving foster care find education, employment, housing, healthcare, mentoring, and other services. The order says it will also expand partnerships with faith-based organizations and address state and local policies that block qualified people or groups from federally funded child-welfare programs because of religious beliefs or moral convictions.

14360.s: This order changes the scope of the reciprocal tariffs so certain agricultural products are no longer subject to them. It also updates the U.S. tariff schedule and allows refunds of duties if needed under applicable law. The changes apply to covered goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after November 13, 2025.

14361.s: This order changes the tariff rules for some goods from Brazil under the earlier emergency order on Brazil. It says certain agricultural products will no longer be subject to the additional 40 percent duty. It also updates the U.S. tariff schedule and allows refunds of duties collected as needed under the law.

14362.s: This order starts a process to consider certain Muslim Brotherhood chapters or other subdivisions for designation as foreign terrorist organizations and specially designated global terrorists. It directs the Secretary of State and the Secretary of the Treasury to review chapters in Lebanon, Jordan, and Egypt and submit a report to the President. If the review leads to designation, the departments must take appropriate action under the law.

14363.s: This order creates the Genesis Mission, a national effort to speed up artificial intelligence use for scientific discovery and research. It directs the Secretary of Energy to build and run the American Science and Security Platform, which will use federal scientific datasets, computing resources, and other tools for AI research. It also calls for coordination with other agencies, universities, businesses, and research facilities, and it applies to federal research resources and participating partners.

14364.s: This order tells the Attorney General and the Federal Trade Commission to set up task forces to investigate food-related industries. They are to look for anti-competitive behavior in the food supply chain and whether foreign control of food-related industries is raising food costs or creating a national or economic security threat. If they find anti-competitive behavior, they are to take steps to remedy it, including enforcement actions, new regulatory approaches, and criminal proceedings when appropriate.

14365.s: This order says the United States should use a minimally burdensome national policy framework for artificial intelligence. It directs federal officials to challenge State AI laws that conflict with this policy, review existing State AI laws, and consider limits on some federal funding for States with those laws. It also directs steps toward a Federal reporting and disclosure standard for AI models and asks for a legislative recommendation for a uniform Federal framework.

14366.s: This order directs the SEC, FTC, and Labor Department to review and possibly revise rules and guidance about proxy advisors. It focuses on proxy advisors' recommendations, conflicts of interest, transparency, and possible antitrust or fraud issues. It also directs the Labor Department to look at how proxy advisors affect pension and retirement plans covered by ERISA.

14367.s: This order designates illicit fentanyl and its core precursor chemicals as weapons of mass destruction. It directs federal agencies to take action against fentanyl trafficking, including investigations, prosecutions, and actions against related assets and financial institutions. It also directs updates to Armed Forces directives for chemical incidents and asks Homeland Security to identify fentanyl smuggling networks.

14368.s: This order sets new pay rates for federal employees under several pay systems, including the General Schedule, the Foreign Service Schedule, and Veterans Health Administration schedules. It also sets pay for senior executives, certain executive, legislative, and judicial offices, uniformed services members, cadets and midshipmen, administrative law judges, and locality-based comparability payments. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management is directed to assess whether certain federal civilian law enforcement personnel should get up to a total pay increase of 3.8 percent.

14369.s: This order directs the government to pursue a space policy focused on exploration, security, commercial growth, and new space technology. It calls for returning Americans to the Moon by 2028, setting up initial parts of a permanent lunar outpost by 2030, and developing next-generation missile defense technology. It also directs agencies to improve space acquisitions, strengthen space security with allies and partners, and revise or revoke earlier space policy directives and orders.

14370.s: This order directs the Attorney General to finish the rulemaking process to reschedule marijuana to Schedule III. It also directs officials to work with Congress on the definition of final hemp-derived cannabinoid products and to develop a regulatory framework for those products. Health agencies are directed to develop research methods and models using real-world evidence to improve access to hemp-derived cannabinoid products and inform standards of care.

14371.s: This order closes executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2025, and December 26, 2025. Their employees are excused from duty on those days. Agency heads may keep certain offices open and require some employees to work for reasons of national security, defense, or other public need. The order also treats those dates as covered by rules on pay and leave for federal employees.

14372.s: This order tells the Secretary of War to identify defense contractors that are underperforming, not investing enough in production capacity, or not prioritizing U.S. government contracts. It says contractors found in that category may get notice, a chance to submit a remediation plan, and possible enforcement actions if the problems are not fixed. It also directs future defense contracts to ban stock buy-backs and corporate distributions during periods of underperformance, and to tie executive pay to on-time delivery and increased production.

14373.s: This order declares a national emergency over certain funds held by the United States for the Government of Venezuela. It bars attachment, judgments, liens, and other judicial process against those funds unless authorized, and it also stops the funds from being transferred or dealt in except as allowed under the order. The funds are described as money from the sale of natural resources or diluents for Venezuela or its agencies. The Secretary of the Treasury and the Secretary of State are given roles in holding and directing the use of the funds.

14374.s: This order creates a second emergency board to investigate and report on disputes between the Long Island Rail Road Company and certain employees represented by several labor organizations. The board will have three members appointed by the President. The parties must submit final offers within 30 days after the board is created, and the board must then send its report to the President within 30 days after those offers are submitted. Until 60 days after the board submits its report, the parties may not change the conditions tied to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

14375.s: This order designates the Board of Peace as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. That gives it certain privileges, exemptions, and immunities under that law. The order says it does not change the authority of executive departments or agencies, and it must be carried out under applicable law and available appropriations.

14376.s: This order directs federal agencies to limit their role in helping large institutional investors buy single-family homes that could otherwise be bought by individual owner-occupants. It tells agencies to promote sales to individual homebuyers and allows narrow exceptions for certain build-to-rent properties and other exceptions the agencies decide are appropriate. It also calls for a review of rules on these investors, antitrust review of their home purchases, and more disclosure from owners and managers of single-family home rentals in federal housing assistance programs.

14377.s: This order directs federal agencies to speed up rebuilding for homes and businesses in the Pacific Palisades and Eaton Canyon wildfire areas. It tells them to consider regulations that would override state or local permitting rules that have delayed the use of federal emergency-relief funds, and to use self-certification for health and safety standards. It also directs agencies to speed up federal permits and reviews, submit legislative proposals, and review California’s use of certain FEMA grant funds.

14378.s: This order keeps the Federal Emergency Management Agency Review Council in place until March 25, 2026. It also says the Secretary of Homeland Security will carry out the President’s functions under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for the council, using rules set by the Administrator of General Services. It takes effect on January 24, 2026.

14379.s: This order creates the White House Great American Recovery Initiative to respond to addiction, also called substance use disorder. It is co-chaired by the Secretary of Health and Human Services and the Senior Advisor for Addiction Recovery, and it includes several other federal officials. The group will recommend ways to coordinate the federal response, increase awareness, help Americans get treatment, and bring prevention, treatment, recovery support, and re-entry into related public programs. It also directs the group to work with states, tribal nations, local governments, community groups, faith groups, private groups, and philanthropic entities.

14380.s: This order declares a national emergency over the Government of Cuba and says Cuba poses a threat to U.S. national security and foreign policy. It allows an extra tariff on goods imported from countries that directly or indirectly sell or provide oil to Cuba. The Secretary of Commerce and the Secretary of State are directed to monitor this issue and make related findings and recommendations, and the Secretary of State is directed to report to Congress.

14381.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Transportation to designate a route in Washington, D.C., for an INDYCAR street race within 14 days. It also tells them to help get the permits and other approvals needed to plan and hold the Freedom 250 Grand Prix. The order says the race route may use roads, trails, or bridges, and that unmanned aircraft systems and other aerial photography may be used by properly permitted people.

14382.s: This order says the government may impose an additional tariff on goods imported into the United States from any country that directly or indirectly buys goods or services from Iran. The Secretary of Commerce must find whether a foreign country does this, and the Secretary of State then decides whether and how much extra duty should be imposed. It affects foreign countries that trade for goods or services from Iran and the goods they export to the United States.

14383.s: This order directs the government to use arms sales and transfers as a tool of foreign policy and to expand U.S. defense production capacity. It tells the Secretary of War, the Secretary of State, and the Secretary of Commerce to create a strategy, a sales catalog, industry recommendations, and a task force to coordinate arms transfer work. It also requires new steps for end-use monitoring, third-party transfer review, advance notice to allies and partners, and quarterly performance metrics on FMS cases and export licenses.

14384.s: This order removes the extra 25 percent duty on products of India imported into the United States on or after February 7, 2026. It says India has committed to stop directly or indirectly importing Russian Federation oil, buy United States energy products, and expand defense cooperation with the United States. It also directs U.S. agencies to carry out the change and to monitor whether India starts importing Russian oil again.

14385.s: This order says the United States will protect its welfare and security from criminal actors, including some foreign nationals with criminal histories. It directs the Attorney General to give DHS access to criminal history record information for screening and vetting, to the extent allowed by law. It also lets DHS share felony conviction records with certain foreign countries for border security and immigration purposes, with reciprocity and privacy safeguards.

14386.s: This order says the United States should keep the electric grid resilient and reliable, and says coal is essential to national and economic security. It directs the Secretary of War, with the Secretary of Energy, to seek long-term power purchase agreements or similar contracts with coal-fired facilities to serve Department of War installations or other mission-critical facilities. The agreements are to focus on grid reliability, fuel security, and mission assurance for defense and intelligence capabilities.

14387.s: This order says elemental phosphorus and glyphosate-based herbicides are important to national defense and agriculture. It gives the Secretary of Agriculture authority to use Defense Production Act powers to keep a continued and adequate supply of those materials and to set nationwide priorities and allocations. Domestic producers of elemental phosphorus and glyphosate-based herbicides must comply with the order.

14388.s: This order keeps the duty-free de minimis exemption from applying to shipments of articles not covered by 50 U.S.C. 1702(b), no matter their value, country of origin, or how they enter the United States. It says such shipments must pay applicable duties, taxes, fees, exactions, and charges, including shipments sent through the international postal network. It also directs Customs and Border Protection and the Secretary of Homeland Security to carry out the new rules.

14389.s: This order ends certain additional ad valorem duties imposed under IEEPA in several earlier executive orders. Federal agencies must begin taking steps to stop collecting those duties as soon as practicable. It does not change other duties, and the national emergencies named in those orders remain in effect.

14390.s: This order directs federal agencies to review how to better fight cybercrime, fraud, and predatory schemes tied to foreign transnational criminal organizations. It calls for an action plan to detect, disrupt, investigate, and dismantle these groups, and for more coordination with the private sector and state, local, Tribal, and territorial partners. It also directs support for victims, continued prosecutions of cyber-enabled fraud cases, and international pressure on foreign governments that allow these activities.

14391.s:
This order changes some Defense Production Act delegations made in a prior order. It gives both the Secretary of Commerce and the Secretary of Energy authority to exercise the delegated power independently of each other.
It also says an agency head only needs to recommend action to the President under a separate order when the President alone has the authority and that authority has not been delegated.

14392.s: This order tells the Federal Trade Commission to focus on enforcing the law against false claims that products are "Made in America" or "Made in the U.S.A." It also tells the FTC to consider rules for online marketplaces that do not verify country-of-origin claims. Agencies with country-of-origin labeling oversight are told to consider rules that support voluntary labeling for products made in the United States. Agencies that buy products for the government must check these claims and remove products if contractors or vendors misrepresent where they are made.

14393.s: This order directs federal agencies to consider changes that would reduce mortgage lending rules and paperwork, especially for smaller banks and community banks. It would affect mortgage borrowers, mortgage lenders, and housing finance agencies by changing rules on loan underwriting, disclosure, servicing, appraisals, digital signatures, enforcement, and licensing. It also calls for steps to improve access to mortgage credit for creditworthy borrowers, including rural and low- and moderate-income households.

14394.s: This order directs federal agencies to review and revise rules tied to stormwater, wetlands, water bodies, energy efficiency, water use, and alternative energy requirements that affect housing construction. It also tells agencies to streamline federal permitting for housing and related infrastructure, like roads, water, and sewer projects. The order asks HUD to set best practices for state and local governments to speed up housing approvals and reduce costs, and it directs Treasury and HUD to look at ways to align Opportunity Zone incentives with more single-family home construction.

14395.s: This order creates a task force in the Executive Office of the President to fight fraud, waste, and abuse in Federal benefit programs. It brings together the Vice President, the Federal Trade Commission chairman, and representatives from several federal agencies. The task force will work on stronger eligibility checks, anti-fraud rules, data sharing, and steps to stop improper payments. Agencies that run these programs must give the task force information and submit plans and descriptions of fraud-prone processes.

14396.s: This order directs the Secretary of Commerce and the Chairman of the FCC to work with the College Football Playoff Committee, the NCAA, and others to create an exclusive broadcast window for the Army-Navy Game. During that window, no other college football game would be broadcast. It also tells the FCC chairman to consider whether public interest rules for broadcast licensees should require the Army-Navy Game to remain a national service event.

14397.s: This order continues the Federal Emergency Management Agency Review Council until 10 days after the required report is sent to the President, or May 29, 2026, whichever comes first. It also says the Secretary of Homeland Security will carry out the President’s functions under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for the council.

14398.s: This order tells federal agencies to add a contract clause barring federal contractors and their subcontractors from racially discriminatory DEI activities. It requires contractors to give records and reports to show compliance, and it allows contracts to be canceled, suspended, or terminated if they do not comply. It also directs agencies to review compliance, issue guidance, and update federal procurement rules to match the order.

14399.s: This order directs federal agencies to help verify citizenship for federal election voting and to share state citizenship lists with state election officials. It also directs the Postal Service to start rulemaking on mail-in and absentee ballot envelopes, tracking, and state participation lists. The order tells the Attorney General to prioritize investigations and prosecutions for issuing ballots to people who are not eligible to vote in a federal election.

14400.s: This order directs federal agencies to act on college sports rules for federally funded higher education institutions. It defines improper financial activities, bars the use of Federal funds for certain NIL and revenue-sharing payments, and tells agencies to consider rule violations when reviewing grants and contracts. It also calls for rules on eligibility, transfers, medical care, revenue sharing, and a national student-athlete agent registry, and it directs the Attorney General to pursue actions against certain State laws that conflict with those rules.

14401.s: This order directs federal agencies to speed review and approval paths for certain psychedelic drugs used for serious mental illness. It also tells FDA and DEA to help eligible patients access these drugs under the Right to Try Act, including ibogaine compounds. The order directs Health and Human Services to use at least $50 million from existing funds to work with state governments on these programs, and it calls for more collaboration with the Department of Veterans Affairs and the private sector.

14402.s: This order directs executive branch agencies to use fixed-price contracts as the default when they buy goods or services, when allowed by law. If an agency uses a non-fixed-price contract, the contracting officer must justify it in writing, and larger contracts need written approval from the agency head. Agency heads must also review their 10 largest non-fixed-price contracts, try to move them toward fixed-price terms, and report those contracts and justifications to the Office of Management and Budget.

14403.s: This order tells the Treasury Secretary to create TrumpIRA.gov by January 1, 2027. The website must give information about high-quality, low-cost IRAs, mainly for independent contractors, self-employed people, and other workers without an employer retirement plan. It also says eligible people who contribute to qualifying IRAs may receive a Federal Saver's Match contribution of up to $1,000. The order directs federal agencies to promote these savings options, set worker-protection rules, and prepare legislative recommendations.

14404.s: This order blocks property of certain foreign persons linked to the Government of Cuba, including people tied to Cuban sectors, people who help the Cuban government, and people involved in serious human rights abuse or corruption in Cuba. It also blocks property of adult family members of covered people and can restrict entry into the United States for some of these persons. The order lets the Treasury Department act against foreign financial institutions that do significant business for blocked persons.

14405.s: This order directs federal financial regulators to review rules, guidance, and application processes that may block fintech firms from entering partnerships with regulated financial institutions or getting licenses and charters. It also asks them to look for ways to streamline access to financial products and services while considering safety, consumer protection, market integrity, and financial stability. The order also asks the Federal Reserve to review access to Reserve Bank payment accounts and payment services for uninsured depository institutions and non-bank financial companies, including those involved in digital assets and other novel financial activities.

14406.s: This order directs the Treasury Department to issue an advisory on risks tied to non-work authorized populations and their employers, including certain fraud, money laundering, and payroll tax evasion patterns. It also directs Treasury and federal financial regulators to consider changes to Bank Secrecy Act rules to strengthen customer due diligence and customer identification requirements. The order asks regulators to consider credit risks tied to non-work authorized borrowers, including possible deportation and loss of wages, when looking at ability to repay.

14407.s: This order directs HHS to review a scientific assessment and, if allowed by law, update the childhood and adolescent vaccine schedule. It says agencies should align their actions, rules, funding, and coverage with the ACIP vaccine schedule adopted by the CDC. It also says the government should keep protecting religious freedom, parental authority, and legal protections for parents, and share the policy with state health officials.

14408.s: This order rescinds two prior executive orders about off-road vehicle use on Federal lands. It directs the Secretary of War, the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Agriculture, the Tennessee Valley Authority, and other relevant agencies to start rulemaking to rescind or revise the regulations that were based on those orders. It says the change is meant to replace those rules with a framework based on existing statutory authorities for managing Federal lands.

14409.s: This order tells federal agencies to strengthen cybersecurity for government systems and critical infrastructure, and to support tools that detect AI-related vulnerabilities. It also creates a voluntary framework for AI developers to work with the federal government on "covered frontier models" and early access for trusted partners. The order directs enforcement against people who use AI to illegally access or damage computer systems or commit other crimes.

14410.s: This order creates and implements Schedule Policy/Career in the excepted service for certain federal jobs with confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating duties. It moves the listed positions into that schedule and requires agencies to notify employees and update their records. It also changes hiring, removal, probation, and award rules for employees in these positions.

14411.s: This order directs the government to tighten customs enforcement and change rules for importers of record. It would require more asset, bond, and disclosure information from importers, block foreign importers of record from filing informal entries, and add stricter rules for some formal entries. It also calls for stronger vetting, more audits and penalties, faster disposal of noncompliant imports, and new transparency reports.

14412.s: This order directs federal agencies to move their information systems to post-quantum cryptography, or PQC, for key establishment and digital signatures. It requires each agency to name a PQC migration lead and have plans for the transition, and it directs OMB to issue guidance for agencies. It also directs NIST to start a PQC migration pilot, and it calls for help to critical infrastructure owners and operators and new contract rules for covered contractors.

14413.s: This order directs federal agencies to update the National Quantum Strategy and coordinate policies to support quantum research, manufacturing, commercialization, and use. It sets up efforts to develop a quantum computer for scientific discovery, improve quantum sensors and networks, and strengthen domestic quantum supply chains. It also calls for steps to protect quantum technology, expand the quantum workforce, and coordinate with international partners.

14414.s: This order directs federal agencies to promote regenerative agriculture, precision agriculture, and farm modernization. It tells the EPA to prioritize certain registration actions and review data on pre-harvest desiccation uses, and it tells Agriculture and HHS to speed up research on chemical exposure in the food supply. It also directs the Department of Agriculture to maximize funding for the Regenerative Pilot Program and look for ways to expand it. Farmers, ranchers, researchers, and federal agencies are the main ones affected.

14415.s: This order directs the Department of War to strengthen defense supply chains and favor materials and components sourced in the United States or from allied nations. It limits waivers for covered materials, unless a contractor submits an accepted mitigation plan, and it says contractors may have to qualify and use alternative sources when they rely on unreliable foreign suppliers. It also requires contractors to map critical supply chains, report supply chain risks, and provide regular reports on the actions taken under the order.

14416.s: This order directs several federal officials to use available authorities to promote the policy of the order and restore trust in the Smithsonian Institution. It also requires temporary signs near the National Museum of American History that tell visitors about the report’s findings and point them to accurate information about American history. The order also requires temporary exhibits or signs that correct inaccurate information in the museum.

14417.s: This order creates the President's Military Spouse Commission to advise and assist the President on policies that affect military spouses and families. The commission will look at issues like housing, employment, healthcare, education, and support related to deployment, and it will recommend actions to help their well-being and quality of life. It will include the spouse of the Secretary of War as chair and other military spouses listed in the order, and it will end after 2 years unless extended.

14418.s: This order directs federal departments and agencies not to issue or accept documents recognizing United States citizenship for certain people when neither parent is a citizen. It applies when a parent is an alien enemy, a foreign government employee, or when citizenship was bought or obtained through fraud. It also applies to people born in certain U.S. territories or territorial waters where citizenship is not given by federal law.

14419.s: This executive order directs the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Homeland Security to take steps against “birth tourism,” which it defines as entering the United States on a nonimmigrant visa for the purpose of giving birth, or helping someone do so. It says they may prevent entry, deny or revoke visas or travel authorization, permanently bar entry, or remove people who have engaged or plan to engage in birth tourism. It also allows exemptions on humanitarian grounds or when entry is in the national interest.

14420.s: This order sets out federal “Gold Standard Childhood Vaccine Recommendations” for childhood and adolescent vaccines and tells federal departments and agencies to review them and take steps to advance them within the law. It says the recommendations should align with scientific evidence and best practices from peer, developed countries while preserving access to vaccines now available to Americans. It also directs HHS to present plans on single-vaccine options, vaccine timing, safer adjuvants, and better safety monitoring, and it tells the Justice Department and other agencies to work on parental authority, religious freedom, disability accommodations, and exemptions from immunization requirements.

14421.s: This order declares a national emergency over threats tied to the foreign supply of bulk-power system electric equipment. It prohibits certain acquisitions, imports, transfers, and installations of foreign-produced equipment when the Secretary of Energy finds it poses risks to the bulk-power system, critical infrastructure, the economy, or national security. It also lets the Secretary set rules for existing equipment, including steps to identify, isolate, monitor, secure, disconnect, replace, or remove it. The order directs changes to federal procurement rules for energy infrastructure and would affect people and companies involved with this equipment and related federal purchases.

14422.s: This order directs the federal government to rename the body of water currently known as Lake Ontario as Lake America. It tells the Secretary of the Interior and the Board on Geographic Names to update federal geographic records and remove references to Lake Ontario from the GNIS. It also says federal maps, contracts, and other documents and communications should use the new name.

14423.s: This order creates a Presidential Commission to study proposals for a United States Space Academy, which would be a NASA-led Federal academy. The commission will look at how the academy should be run, what it should teach, who can apply, and what service obligations graduates should have. It must also recommend any laws or administrative steps needed to set up the academy.

14424.s: This order directs the Agriculture Department to step up enforcement of the Packers and Stockyards Act against unfair, discriminatory, deceptive, or price-manipulating practices in livestock and meat markets. It also calls for more resources, more coordination with the Justice Department, and a report on enforcement actions and needs. The order aims to expand interstate market access for meat products, including more state inspection program participation, technical help for small processors, a USDA web resource, and a loan program for small and regional beef processors. It affects ranchers, small and medium meat processors, and consumers of meat products.

14425.s: This order tells several agencies to review rules and policies that affect ranchers and to make recommendations to support their financial viability and market access. It directs the Interior Department to look at gray wolf and Mexican wolf recovery status and consider changes related to delisting, livestock predation, depredation claims, and wolf removal. It also directs Agriculture to review whether mandatory country-of-origin labeling for beef products can be established and to consider rules or legislative recommendations. The order says the measures should be carried out in a way that helps American consumers through lower prices as much as possible.

14426.s: This order directs the Department of War and the Department of Veterans Affairs to share military personnel files and medical records more quickly. It also calls for new digital tools to help veterans apply for benefits and find job training and job opportunities. The order requires updates to job transition programs so service members leaving active duty are connected to open jobs, training, apprenticeships, and veterans' representatives who can help with benefit applications.

14427.s: This order changes how some powers under the Defense Production Act are delegated. It gives the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Energy, and the Secretary of Commerce certain authorities, and says some of those powers may be used independently of one another. It also sets rules for handling disputes between the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Energy over energy matters, including referral to the National Energy Dominance Council and, in some cases, the National Security Council and the Department of War.

14428.s: This order revokes Executive Order 13508 and sets new directions for federal work on the Chesapeake Bay. It tells certain federal agencies to focus resources on direct projects that improve water quality and reduce nutrient and sediment runoff. It also directs the Environmental Protection Agency to work with Maryland, Virginia, Pennsylvania, Delaware, New York, West Virginia, and the District of Columbia on stormwater management fees and on options that do not increase costs for residents.

14429.s: This order directs federal agencies to expand hunting and other outdoor access on certain federal lands, including allowing hunting in Castle Mountains National Monument and Craters of the Moon National Monument and Preserve for species not subject to listed protections. It also calls for changes to policies on access, hunter education, river access lotteries, migratory game bird hunting, and Sunday hunting opportunities. The order also asks agencies to work on growing game species populations and supporting wild game donation programs.

14430.s:
This order tells federal agencies to put more weight on recreational fishing in ocean, coastal, and public land decisions. It directs them to modernize fishing data collection, use mobile reporting, and review rules and permit practices that affect anglers, charter operators, and outdoor businesses.
It also sets up work on artificial reefs, predator depredation, and projects to increase fish abundance. The order affects federal agencies, states, private partners, anglers, charter operators, and related coastal industries.

14431.s: This order directs several federal agencies to coordinate when reviewing H-1B petitions, labor condition applications, and visas. It says they must check whether sponsoring employers have had layoffs in the past year or plan future layoffs that affect similarly situated United States workers. It also tells the Labor Department to start reviewing prior labor condition application data for possible further action.

14432.s: This order directs the creation of America.gov as a single online entry point for people in the United States seeking Federal information or services. It would let users sign in, get answers in plain language, and, where allowed, complete covered Federal transactions through one place instead of moving across multiple agency websites. The order applies to covered services that serve more than 100,000 users in a 12-month period and can be accessed or applied for online, but it excludes IRS tax filing services and services from the Department of War and the Intelligence Community. It also says Americans may still use in-person, telephone, mail, and agency-specific digital services.

14433.s: This order directs federal agencies to develop and carry out a campaign in the District of Columbia to reduce invasive mosquito and tick populations. It also calls for new ways to detect, prevent, and treat diseases spread by ticks and mosquitoes, including Lyme disease, West Nile, Zika, Chikungunya, and Dengue fever. The order asks agencies to explore non-chemical control methods, including advanced technologies, and to review options for labeling food and drug products that contain significant amounts of alpha-galactose.

14434.s:
This order directs executive departments and agencies to use “Super Intelligence” and “SI” instead of “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI” in official correspondence, public communications, websites, reports, policy documents, and other non-statutory documents. It says this change does not require changing past regulations, presidential actions, contracts, grants, or other historical documents.

It also defines “Super Intelligence” and “SI” as the technologies and systems covered by the federal definition of “artificial intelligence.” Within 60 days, the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology must submit proposed legislative language for a federal definition and related changes.

14435.s: This order directs the Treasury Secretary to consider deferring certain diesel fuel tax payments and to provide penalty relief if allowed by law. It also directs the IRS to announce that it will not impose certain penalties for dyed diesel fuel sold for use or used on the highway during the stated period. The order also tells Agriculture and Transportation to help carry out the policy, and it affects farmers, truckers, workers, and other taxpayers covered by the relief.

14436.s: This order carries out the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. It raises duties on goods from the Russian Federation and on goods from the largest 5 importers of Russian crude oil and natural gas if they make new purchases after the listed date, and on the top 5 countries that help evade Russian oil sanctions. It also waives some sanctions, restrictions, and duties under the law for now, and directs officials to monitor Russian oil and gas imports and sanctions evasion.

14437.s: This order directs the Health and Human Services Secretary, through NIH, to establish a Women's Health Division within 90 days. It also creates a White House Women's Health Task Force to coordinate federal work on women's health research, care, and policy across all stages of life. The order affects federal agencies working on health, research, and related programs, and it revokes two prior executive actions on women's health research.

14438.s: This order directs federal housing agencies to reduce regulatory barriers that affect mortgage origination and homeownership costs. It sets up a pilot program to review mortgages for possible mortgage insurance cancellation, creates a task force on manufactured housing and factory-built homes, and expands a title review program for certain refinance loans. It also directs the Agriculture and Veterans Affairs departments to reduce interest rates on single-family direct home loans, consistent with law and available appropriations.
